*61. SHRI YASHWANT SINHA: Will
the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a South Summit meeting
was held at Doha in June, 2005;
(b) whether it is a fact that neither the
Prime Minister nor the Minister of External
Affairs attended this Summit meeting; and
(c) whether as a result thereof India
missed a great opportunity to promote its
case for a permanent seat in the UNSC
with the members of G-77?

†*62. PROF R. B. S. VARMA:
SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL:
Will the Minister of OCEAN

(a) whether it is a fact that a team of
Indian Scientists is being sent by
Government to Antarctica for research work;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the subject on which the Indian
Scientists would undertake research at
Antarctica; and
(d) by when, the task would be
completed?

(a) the number of vehicles running on
authorized L.P.G. in the country, State-wise;
(b) the number of  L.P.G. filling stations
in the country, State-wise, to meet the
requirement of such vehicles;

Corruption in SAI
*64. SHRI  PRAMOD MAHAJAN:
SHRI R. K. ANAND:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Auditors
of Sports Authority of India have written
to Government alleging corruption in SAI;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the action taken thereon?
Installation of STD/ISD/PCO booths
*65. PROF. M. M. AGARWAL: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) the number of STD/ISD/PCOs
running in the various districts of Uttar

Corruption in administration
†*66. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the general
public of the country has to spend
Rs. 21,068 crores annually in the form of
bribe to solve their general problems;
(b) if so, the reaction of Government in
this regard;
(c) whether Government have reformed
the administrative functioning to remove
corruption from the administration during
the past years; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Target of Golden Quadrilateral
*67. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the
Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) the extent of achievement of targets
by end of the year 2005 of first phase
(NHDP) of road development plan—
Golden Quadrilateral, involving four or six
laning of 5,846 KM of National Highways
between Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and
Kolkata;
(b) the percentage of work that remains
to be done and its location; and
(c) the steps Government are
adopting to achieve completion by the target
date?
Indo-China border talks
*68. SHRI MOOLCHAND
MEENA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether China has expressed its
readiness to solve boundary issue with
India on the basis of equility and
with mutual understanding and
concessions;
(b) whether this was expressed by
Chinese Chief of Army who had

21
discussions with National Security
Advisor, recently in India;
(c) if so, whether both India and China
have now agreed to mutually settle this
issue;
(d) if so, the latest progress in solving
the issue and whether Governments of
India and China have agreed to have
settlement on this border issue; and
(e) by when the final agreement in this
regard is likely to be reached?
Charges for money orders
*69. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN:
Will the Minister of COMMUNICA-
TIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the charges for
sending money orders are exorbitantly high;
(b) if so, what steps Government
propose to take to rationalize these charges;
and
(c) whether Government would examine
the feasibility of finding out cost-effective
ways of sending money orders or its
substitutes?
Commercial launching by ISRO
*70. SHRI R. SHUNMUGASUN-
DARAM: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any
proposal for commercial launching by
ISRO;
(b) by when the said commercial launch
is likely to commence; and
(c) whether there would be any tie-up
with other countries in such commercial
launching?
Discussion on Global Warming in G-8
Summit
*71. SHRI R. S. GAVAI:
SHRI MANOJ
BHATTACHARYA:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a conference
of industrial nations of the world was held
recently in Scotland;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the details of the discussion held
with regard to global warming;
(d) what steps would be taken to check
this problem;
(e) whether the developed countries
agreed to reduce the increasing Green House
emissions; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Debt burden of Orissa
*72. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that Orissa State has an accumulated
debt burden of Rs. 31,636 crores as on 31st
March, 2005;
(b) whether Government are also aware
of progress made by Orissa State in reining
in its deficits through tough and difficult
steps;
(c) whether the cash-strapped State has
requested the Centre to grant them
monthly allocation of its plan assistance
and share of Central taxes, as the State has
no resources to meet its part of obligation
for development works; and

22
(d) if so, the action plan of the Centre
to help the State to overcome the current
financial condition?
Provision of low cost personal
computers
*73. SHRIMATI  S. G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are considering to provide low cost personal
computers;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that for the
below Rs. 10,000 computers, Government
desires financing packages as well as suitable
policies to ensure their mass production;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Diversion of funds
*74. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of LABOUR
AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) the total corpus in the Employees
Provident Fund at present;
(b) whether Government are investing
certain portion of the fund in stocks and
shares;
(c) if so, the details, of stocks and shares
in which the funds are invested;
(d) whether Government are considering
to divert a portion of the funds for granting
pension to the contributors and for
undertaking certain social welfare activities,
like setting up of technical institutions,
hospitals, labour intensive commercial
activities, etc.;
(e) if so, the details in this regard; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?
Telephone booths at ration shops
*75. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal to
establish telephone booths at public
distribution shops (ration shops);
(b) if so, whether the proposal has been
accepted by the State Governments;
(c) if so, the details including the number
of such booths proposed to be set up, State-
wise and category-wise as on today; and
(d) if so, the State Governments which
have accepted the above proposal as on
date?
Plans to meet future coal demand
*76. SHRI K. B. KRISHNA
MURTHY:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that his Ministry
has not formulated any plan to meet future
coal demand;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
ensure availability of adequate quantity of
coal to core sectors like power generation,
steel, aluminium and infrastructure?
Hurriyat leaders' Pakistan visit
without passport
*77. SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI:
SHRI YASHWANT SINHA:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Hurriyat
delegation which crossed the Line of

23
Control by Muzaffarabad bus was allowed
to go to Islamabad without passport and
visa;
(b) whether it is not a violation of the
Indo-Pak agreement;
(c) what protests Government
have made with the Government of
Pakistan;
(d) what steps are being taken to see
that this does not become a precedence;
and
(e) whether Government was fully
aware of the invitation of the Government
of Pakistan to the Hurriyat leaders to visit
Pakistan and still allowed them to travel to
Pakistan through Muzaffarabad without
passports and visas?
Local dialling within States
*78. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether in certain States like Tamil
Nadu, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, etc.
telephone subscribers do not have to dial
'0' to access mobile phones in another circle
within the State from both mobile phones
and landline phones;
(b) whether this facility is likely to be
extended from landline to landline phones
also;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Regulator for coal pricing
*79. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY:
SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have decided to establish a regulator for
coal pricing;
(b) what impact it would have on the
cost of generation of power in the country;
(c) whether the proposal has been
scrutinised by the Tariff Commission; and
(d) if so, what are the reommendations
of the Tariff Commission on the proposed
framework on coal pricing?
Chinese support to India's claim for
UNSC seat
*80. SHRI B. K. HARIPRASAD:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether India has secured support
from many nations for its candidacy to a
permanent seat in UN Security Council
under the G-4 Umbrella;
(b) whether during his recent visit to
India, the Chinese Premier had expressed
support for India's bid for a Security
Council seat; and
(c) if so, whether the reported Chinese
support comes with a rider that India should
abandon the company of other G-4
member, Japan, whose relations with China
is at its lowest ebb?

technology which allows television, phone

willing to push this technology as the most
preferred one for rural areas; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?

made in this respect?

Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
